metadata.notes: Q/PAX/FNG data reflects only what was recorded in backblast text as posted by Qs; it is backblast-observed participation, not a complete membership or attendance record. A PAX's absence from these records does not mean they did not attend F3 events, and a PAX's first appearance here is not proof of an FNG/start date unless a backblast explicitly identifies them as an FNG. This is an immutable archive chunk of the full backblast knowledge base; it is written once and never re-pulled or rewritten. See f3-nation-backblasts-latest.json for the newest, still-updating records.

Step outside your comfort zone and foster “Shield Locks” to support your development mentally and spiritually. I’m thankful for each and everyone of you in my life. backblasts.announcements: COT: YHC was dreading getting out for F3 this morning, mainly due to the weather but also knowing we wouldn't get much, if any, of the PAX out. Once out on the field, it occurred to YHC that the anticipation of a challenge or uncomfortable experience was much worse than the experience itself. Once I was outside and moving, it was rather fun. Had the whole of Hiawatha to myself and the wind and rain only motivated me to keep moving and stay warm. So it was a good lesson to minimize the options to think about a challenge ahead of time and back down.

So there’s wisdom in considering how short our lives are and what we put our hope in. Invest in those important to you and your faith. Special thanks to Foley…

backblasts.announcements: COT: Words were shared by @Worthington on the occasion of his son's 21st birthday, who he is flying out to see today. I'm going to let him post his own message here, because I don't think I could do justice to his eloquent words. I shared how a college aptitude test correctly predicted my profession, but the same test, in a way, predicted that I wouldn't be Q'ing today , with off-the-chart low scores for "gym teacher" and "drill instructor". But regardless of aptitude, I'm both humbled and honored to lead this group today, with so many HIMs that have shaped my F3 experience over the past 5 months.

backblasts.announcements: We have lots of announcements going around these days, but none as historic for #ao-counterbalance as the handoff of the SITE Q It is with great pleasure that I hand over the site Q to @Bueller. He's become a recent regular at CB this year, and has gone through many trials and tribulations with the PAX for some time now. He cares deeply for the PAX and pushes guys around him every day to be better (YHC included). I'm super pumped to hand over our crucible for leaders in training to someone who can continue and expand the culture of Counterbalance and help present even greater challenges and feats of Endurance, Strength, and Love for the PAX to conquer for months to come! Thank you @Bueller for taking the helm!

backblasts.cot_summary: WARMUP: none today. Intro by @watson re IPC wk3, named Mrs Burns, with demo of each exercise. THE THANG: The Exercises: 20 each of OH coupon presses, burpees, curls, V-ups & goblet squats then 13 man makers, followed by a 400M run around the track. This routine was repeated 5 X. After the 5th round, the pax ran another 400M lap for a total of 571 reps, which represented the 571 days Mrs Burns courageously battled pancreatic cancer until her death on 8-21-22.

backblasts.announcements: There's a 2ndF pub crawl. Check slack. COT/WoW: Taking the path less traveled is no guarantee. But I encourage others to trust their gut and reject the doubters and critics that will only slow your movement to advantage. I had plenty of those during our move to Arkansas. The same was true in nearly all important life decisions, from my marriage to my service in the Marines to nearly every career move I've made. My only regrets have been letting them in and giving those critics weight and stirring doubt in my heart. Build the relationships that will have your six and help support your journey, not slow your down on your path.

backblasts.cot_summary: The obvious theme of the workout was about partners. I shared that I recently celebrated the 10 year anniversary of losing my first son Noah. It was an unimaginable, heart-wrenching experience that I don’t wish upon anyone, but I am fortunate that I had a partner to get through it with (my wife). I shared a few characteristics of a good partnership that I tried to showcase in today’s workout: communication, recognizing strengths in your partner, and stepping up in your partner’s times of weaknes…

backblasts.announcements: Recap of F3 Family Camping and look forward to dad's weekend in September. Tough Mudder and Spartan Beast. WOW and Prayer: YHC had time to reflect this past weekend at F3 Family Camp about what distinguishes F3 HIMs and came up with 3 things: 1) Humility: A desire to learn from others, a desire to realize that there is value in putting others before yourself, and a commitment to showing up early and doing hard things. 2) A Commitment to be Better: Better fathers, husbands, and men. A Desire to be disciplined and grow in community....a meaningful community. 3) Living BIG: F3 men get off the couch and live life as an adventure and expose their 2.0's and M's to the value of such adventure. Oct 15 More announcements: During Sunday’s discussion, YHC misstated the title of a book which seemed applicable. The correct title is, “The 10X Rule”, by Grant Cardone. Ferrari, you mentioned a book. What was that title? That was a great discussion, gentlemen! Thank you!

backblasts.announcements: -Gear order, see any Tundra AO slack channel -Mens retreat, see Slack or Hansel for details WOW - YHC shared an article that had been shared with me (link: <https://www.nytimes.com/2024/01/19/opinion/religion-ancient-text-judaism.html>). I won’t get into all the details, but one of my takeaways is the importance of showing up. We tend to want to go home and be alone when things are difficult, but it is important to have a community that can help support us during those tough times. I think F3 is a great example of this! But we also need to show up when life is good so that we can be the ones providing support and encouragement. Again F3, in my experience, does this very well. I encouraged us all to take this out into the rest of the day and “show up” for those in our lives, for those other…

backblasts.announcements: Don't forget to check team-up for up coming Q opps WOW. I was taking with a good friend recently sharing how my efforts to raise awareness of feelings over the last couple of years has helped tremendously in parenting, marriage and work. Without awareness, I've personally found myself at times stressed, unhealthy, angry and unhappy and confused on how I ended up there. Track your BEAR. Boredom Entitlement Angst Resentment Put it in a spreadsheet on your phone, give it a point system (if you experience that feeling, you get a point for the day) and if it's above 20 for the week, you are "in the danger zone". Adjust realtime to offset these feelings, track over the weeks and take a vacation, workout more (or less if that is causing resentment with the M), connect with a friend for coffee/bee…

backblasts.cot_summary: YHC spoke of observing his ability to be engaged and present during the holiday season thus far, despite maybe expecting to not be so much, considering it's still less than 3 months since his Mom passed (who was such a big fan of Christmas). Of course, the emotions came back last night and YHC cried himself to sleep. This is part of the process and it's okay. But it's been good to observe myself through this process and take stock in how I'm doing. We should try to do that as much as we're able,…

But as the time ticked ever closer to 5:30, an unease stalked the PAX. _Where was the Q?_ The PAX had been promised JazzHands and yet no JazzHands could be found there. By 5:28, a wailing and gnashing of teeth overcame the PAX, bloodcurdling keens drifting over the goose poop hills. Just before the PAX could begin rending their F3-branded Mudgear shirts in distress, Alimony gathered himself for the greater good…

backblasts.announcements: • Woodinville Beerteria is back in action on February 22 - see the woodinville-beerteria channel for details. • Men's weekend in May at YL Malibu in Canada - check out the mensmalibu channel COT/WoW: Climbing a mountain or even Heart Attack Hill can be intimidating and seemingly insurmountable. But in the dark, you're just focused on the step in front of you and immediately what's next. Eventually you get there by those cumulative thousands of individual steps. It's a great metaphor for life, when a challenge seems impossible - all you need to do is focus on the very next step. Thanks, brothers, for joining me in the gloom!

backblasts.cot_summary: my dad’s health has taken a nose dive the last few months, but he’s been in decline since he retired 15 years ago. He’s never had hobbies or interests, which means too much free time without his job. Having something to look forward to gets you out of bed and keeps your mind sharp.

backblasts.announcements: Next week, on July 14, MooseJaw walks us through chapters 20, 21, & 22. On July 21, Asbestos (F3-The Coeur) finishes out the book with chapters 23 and 24. It’s already time to start thinking about our next book. Share your suggestions in this channel. Final thought: It’s ok to not feel great, right? That’s a normal part of life. But there sometimes comes a time when we could use some help. One word that came up in our conversation today is despair. If you feel this way, or know someone who does, please reach out for help. Call 988. It’s the Lifeline. “There is hope”, but that hope can be hard to see from down in the depths. Men commit suicide 4 times more frequently than women. We must be watchful among the people we know and especially aware of our own needs and situations. YHC is not Glo…

backblasts.name: Backblast! O Brother Where Art Thou
backblasts.announcements: - Irrelevant, this backblast is 2 weeks late! :see_no_evil: COT (Words): - YHC shared the inspiration for the workout, which was a scene in a annoying-at-times kids' show called Super Kitties. It was a surprisingly inspiring moment - one character had to set out on her own to face her fear of the dark in order to complete the mission, and the rest of her team cheered her on as she set out. I love that kind of moment - someone pushing themselves, with their teammates at their back cheering them on - even as they are depending on them to succeed. So we put it into practice with "O Brother Where Art Thou". Be on the lookout for inspiring stories that touch your heart, and be curious about what strikes a chord - you can learn about yourself and enjoy the inspiration! Always an honor to lead, e…

backblasts.announcements: 1. Farewell to Daaa Auditor. We knew this was coming, but its sucks that it finally happened. Seattle will miss every bit of Daaa Auditor, he has been a _HIM_ of the first level, bringing his speed, good nature and sense of humor to many, many Qs. _Happy Trails and Best Wishes to you and your family!!_ 2. Seattle CSLOG is coming in October-- sign up now. WOW - Priceline spoke about staying in the present and focusing on what we can do and not on what we coulda/shoulda done. Alimony shared that he has more joy and less anger and resentment when he stops attempting to be the director, stops demanding his specific outcomes and instead seeks to be one in a family, a friend among friends, a worker among workers and useful to others. It was great to be out in the sunshine with you this morning.…

A bowling ball is designed to have momentum and create impact, so is a man. However, when he neglects his fitness, his relationships and his purpose in life, a man can become like a bowling ball that is unused, stored and covered in dust. An object of immense potential with no inertia or impact. A HIM fills the 3 bowling ball grip holes with fitness, fellowship and service outside of himself so that he can fulfill his potential and create massive impact. It was an honor doing something very hard with you men this morning.

backblasts.cot_summary: Today is my 4th wedding anniversary (Fun Fact: it's also Tater Truck's) and on or around this time each year I like to remind myself that "Love is a choice, not a feeling. Feelings come and go, and if we choose to base our most important relationships on how we feel at any particular moment, we are in for a rough and rocky journey. Love is a verb, not a noun. Love is something we do, not something that happens to us". and remember, F3 is something to give away, every day!

backblasts.cot_summary: Friend of mine has now had cancer three times and now appears to be in remission (again). I reached out a couple of days ago to check in. It had been a couple of months. He immediately called me back. I should have called him sooner. No excuse. Don't wait, check in on your friends. They appreciate it. They need to know you care. I was selfish. Would I want others to check in with me if I was sick? Absolutely. Do the same to others. Lesson learned.

backblasts.name: Backblast! Three Amigoes and their bricks
backblasts.cot_summary: YHC closed with a reflection on the power of positive thinking. More often than not, when we approach life with a positive mindset, the results turn out better than expected. A small but powerful blessing to carry with us beyond the gloom. Moleskin: Not every workout is packed with PAX, but the camaraderie and challenge remain the same. And today, our bricks were solid friends. Until next time! SYITG.

backblasts.announcements: -Poker night at Worthingtons Oct. 26 -Holiday party planning details coming soon, likely first weekend in December WOW - I shared how my wife and I have been working with my 5 year old to handle mistakes/adversity in soccer. It has me reflecting on how I avoid difficult things or don’t handle mistakes well. The PAX were encouraging in offering insight into how to model hard things (i.e. F3) or being open about mistakes with my 2.0s. As an added bonus we had a special coffeeteria at the Juanita McDonalds. Silent B, Copay, and Gremlin demonstrated true HIM behavior helping out Penny, the longtime kingsgate coffee person who now works the Juanita location, with some car troubles.

However the community support has been amazing - neighbors, friends, co-workers, F3 HIMs, etc. What I recognized is that my willingness to give/help out is much stronger than my ability to receive. I have not been able to care and support my family the way I would like the last 10 days, but others have helped step in and filled in the gap. Being able to receive is a muscle that isn't often use…

backblasts.cot_summary: YHC is reading "The Right Stuff" by Tom Wolfe, a novel about the first astronauts. While not entirely factual, it was based off his conversations with test pilots. One of the interesting tendencies the pilots would present is that, when a pilot would die in a crash (an alarmingly common occurrence), they would talk about the mistakes that pilot had made that and how they themselves never would. In doing so, they essentially disregarded the role that luck played in their own survival. But it was…

WOW - In reading a fictional book over break, one scene struck me. An admiral had just arrived on his ship and had to be woken up by an enlisted sailor. The admiral snapped at being woken as he was tired and under a lot of stress. Later he realized that this was poor leadership, taking his stress out on a sailor who was simply doing his duty. Unfortunately I can relate to the admiral's situation, where I let stress from work or elsewhere in my life affect how I interact with my wife or kids, acting out my stress when they don’t deserve it. backblasts.announcements: Extreme week is coming up, kicking off with the Monday AM Convergence at Luther Burbank Park on Mercer Island. Mercer Island: the DMZ between Seattle and The Eastside. If you're on the fence about extreme week, I have this for you: I started F3 in December of 2021, in what I would term "not great shape". (I carried an inhaler for the first 6 months for allergies/wheezing that really got to me while running). Hearing about the Feb 2022 Extreme Week, I was concerned about being physically able to work out every day for a week. But my concern was unfounded. While it was a stretch, I felt my body getting stronger during the week. My advice would be to plan getting more sleep than normal for recovery, but I know that every one of you can do this. The best part was getting to know other HIMs out…

backblasts.announcements: - 10-week challenge folks are seeing positive results, not necessarily weight loss. Sugar is in many things. - Join an Extreme week -- January 31 - February. (7 workouts in 6 days across the Puget Sound area) - Check the Slack Channel: #extreme-week, WOW - I shared that vertigo, confusion, and spatial disorientation are common feelings that we can have during workouts, flying, scuba diving, life in general or increasingly as we get older. It's common to feel uncomfortable, fearful and confused when our bodies perceive things in new or different ways. F3 workouts are great at muscle confusion, encourages muscle and neuron development. We tried a couple of exercises from my brain therapy (post concussions recovery) that hopefully sparked proprioception neurons and our vestibular systems too.…

backblasts.announcements: check slack or talk to Fannie (seems to be more informed than most on happenings in the region -always appreciated at COT). Need more Qs at CoT / WOW: 3 Rs - this is a concept I was introduced to recently while reading a great parenting book titled "Raising Emotionally Strong Boys: Tools Your Son Can Build on for Life". Excellent read for dads of sons. Recognize - recognize what you're feeling. Challenge for the PAX: Buy a feelings wheel on amazon and have everyone go around at dinner and identify one feeling from the day on the outer edge. Great bonding activity. Regulate - once you have identified the feeling, figure out what you need to do to respond in healthy ways (go for a walk, jumprope, speed bag, walk in the grass barefoot...) Repair - if you screw up, that's okay, it happens. But…

backblasts.cot_summary: We are currently in what I affectionately call "birthday season" at the Columbia household. Five birthdays in two months translates to a whirlwind of celebrations. While joyous, these events can be draining. For me personally, it's crucial to recognize the potential for burnout and to prepare accordingly. This means prioritizing self-care, managing expectations, and finding moments of peace amidst the festivities. Pancake get's results back for his bum knee today - we are rooting for ya brother!

She spent the next session mostly talking and building her up, and wouldn't you know it, she had 6 hits at the next tournament and has looked like a different player since. Hollywood chimed in about similar experience with kids tensing up in games, and not playing as freely as scrimmages. Keep it fun!

Don’t expect it from Cheap people” Warren Buffett. Q asked the team for suggestions for the best way to find a job in these days of blind HR departments and computer matching of resumes with job descriptions. backblasts.name: Backblast! misogi
backblasts.announcements: COT: Hyster coming off of the gte talked about the importance of doing hard things and how we tend to come back to them and do them again even after saying we never will. New transmitter and dopamine flood that comes from doing hard things aside. I brought up the concept of misogi which is a Japanese term and ritual for doing incredibly physically difficult challenges and looking at it as a cleansing ritual to be done. I think yearly as a testament to how ingrained doing hard things truly is to humans in general. Go do hard things

backblasts.name: Backblast! Deconstructing Millennials
backblasts.announcements: So many fun things planned. IKEA is throwing the 2nd annual Mabel Pizza Party on August 23rd. M’s and 2.0’s welcome. Alimony will hopefully set sail by the end of the gathering. Iron Pax is coming- all are encouraged to participate, by proctoring or by suffering through the beatdowns Dad Camp is six weeks away. If you have kids, and you want to show them the splendors or Orkila and Gaga Ball, sign up. YHC has done it for or five times, and it is always a great experience. Thanks for the opportunity to lead. Your collective enthusiasm, grit, humor and general bad-assery inspires me. It was an honor to Q, and I look forward to doing it again in another 127 days.

backblasts.announcements: • Sept: IronPAX. Sign up now! • 9/1: Robinswood Monday Morning Mayhem 7AM • 9/19 - 9/21: Dad's Camp • 9/28: Base to Space CoT YHC had a Birthday yesterday, 54. Instead of getting depressed about getting older. I’m excited about what I am doing and what is in the future. This is because I have purpose. As men of this age, we must be vigilant because purpose can slip away when life gets too routine or when we stop pushing ourselves. Keep busy, challenge yourself, help others and work on your passions. This will help keep your sense of purpose. If you do that, you can be excited & celebrate age milestones, not dread them.

backblasts.name: Backblast! Doom Trifecta – 5 Years of Jalapeño Hea
backblasts.announcements: - IPC is in full swing during September. Check disc-ironpax for more info. - Pickleball picnic is tomorrow at 3 pm at Kingsgate — see event-pickleballpicnic - Base to Space is happening September 29. Join @Lumbermac and @Delorean to honor cancer survivors and support research. - Tundra Region Ultra CSAUP is on Saturday, October 4. Register at event-tundra-backyard-ultra-csaup
backblasts.cot_summary: 14 men showed up strong today, not just for a workout but to mark a milestone. Five years ago, I first posted at DOOM and didn’t even know what I was missing. I had no clue what challenges were ahead, but F3 has prepared me for them—and for life—better than I ever could have imagined. Five years later, I’m a stronger, sharper, and better version of myself thanks to the 3Fs this group brings. Grateful for every man who’s been part of the ride, past, present, and future. Here’s to showing up, putt…

backblasts.cot_summary: Delorean shared his father, Juan Olivo Sr., who battled lymphoma during Covid five years ago, has been diagnosed with cancer again. Stepping into circle, shedding a tear, Delorean expressed importance of maintaining relationships with parents; even lamenting how he could have been a better son in retrospect. "I was full of angst at times" Juan said, "like any child growing up. But call your parents. Take the time. Tell them you love them...because you just never know."

backblasts.announcements: Little John will be posting the poll for the next book soon. Get recommendations in NOW if you want. Then vote early and vote often. Here are some books that I either referenced or think would be worth looking at if you want things that are in this relative sphere: - "https://www.elliottbaybook.com/item/FQO0d1ZFIap_QXl9A2BA1A" by Atul Gawande - a book by a surgeon exploring more tangible ways that we do/don't face mortality and aging. This is where the "ice cream and football" example comes from - "https://www.elliottbaybook.com/item/07BW63iqQGLv2lsECm2iVw" - by Donald Miller - this is where the obituary exercise I referenced came from. You can download templates for what he lays out in the book https://hero-on-a-mission-resources.s3.amazonaws.com/Hero+on+a+Mission+Worksheets.pdf?utm_mediu…

backblasts.cot_summary: Procrastination kills. Whether you struggle with ADD or lack of motivation/inspiration or just bad planning, procrastination results in added stress and anxiety and can really affect family dynamics. There are many strategies and techniques to help reduce procrastination, but as we know, it’s hard to execute alone. Get help - whether a medical or mental health professional, and certainly some F3 shieldlock! I ask for your help in accountability for me, as I have been meaning to get evaluated for…

backblasts.cot_summary: Interesting fact. Gordon Lightfoot's song, "The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald" was a response to a typo. The wreck took place on November 10th 1975, and a Newsweek article was written a couple months later, but they named 'Edmond' with an O, instead of with a U. Gordon Lightfoot felt it dishonored the memory of the crew, and wrote the song in response... arguably brining it huge notoriety. Lightfoot's ballad was well received by the families and he took part in many remembrances over the years.…

backblasts.name: Backblast! THE SIX-PACK SHOWS UP AT PERESTROIKA
backblasts.announcements: Thanksgiving Convergence at the Arboretum with Banzai 0530 pre-beatdown On-site breakfast immediately after—absolutely worth it. January 1st Redmond Convergence Polar Plunge included Start the year icy and alive. A few of us, including flexo, berks, side out, Rasputin, and I guess me are signed up for the Lake Sammamish half marathon in march. Join the madness! Words of Wisdom: Have a backup. We all think we can carry everything on our own—until the moment we can’t. And by then, it’s too late to build support. So intentionally cultivate your backups: your Shield Lock, your closest friend, your brother in the gloom. Be someone else’s backup, too. It’s how you stay strong—together. Great morning, Six-Pack. Pure Lead

backblasts.name: Backblast! Silent counts
backblasts.cot_summary: We closed with a reminder about the importance of validating our assumptions and never judging a book by its cover. You never really know what someone is carrying—what stress, hurt, or burden sits behind their smile—until you go out of your way to check in and offer support. It was an honor to serve today, gents. Good to see some familiar faces again after a short hiatus — felt great to be back out there with the crew.

backblasts.name: Backblast! Almost as OG as AP
backblasts.announcements: COT: Response Ability is the space between stimulus and response—the moment of freedom where you choose who you will be. Stephen Covey made it Habit 1. While reactive people are driven by feelings, weather, or others’ behavior, proactive people pause, access their values, and decide. In that pause lies growth, happiness, and power. Life is 10 % what happens to you and 90 % how you respond. Master this space and you master your life. No one can make you angry, offended, or defeated without your consent. Response Ability is not just a skill—it is your ultimate human endowment. Bullwinkle adding some words about leaning into the F3 community.

backblasts.cot_summary: 3 Lessons Learned from Year as Nantan (3 point sermon): 1. Live Life Outside the Comfort Zone There will Never be a time when you will not grow by being stretched beyond your comfort zone. Growth never happens when you never say "yes" to something daunting with a healthy chance of failure. 2) Live with an Abundance Mentality In God's Kingdom there is never a shortage, no hill is too steep, no personal challenge that cannot be overcome, no wound that can't be healed. Paradoxically, there will NEV…
